findings.span: Dose–response analyses will use only participants enrolled in the randomized expansion cohort; data from the escalation cohort, pharmacokinetic substudy, and other sources will be excluded, and no covariate analyses are planned.
findings.claim: Excluding escalation and PK-substudy data discards available evidence needed to characterize dose– and exposure–response and select the RP2D.
findings.guidance_quote: Sponsors should consider all available data when evaluating dose–response and exposure–response relationships to inform dosage selection.

findings.span: Dose–response analyses will use only participants enrolled in the randomized expansion cohort; data from the escalation cohort, pharmacokinetic substudy, and other sources will be excluded, and no covariate analyses are planned.
findings.claim: The plan omits covariate analyses that could identify differences in exposure, efficacy, or toxicity relevant to dosage selection.
findings.guidance_quote: Exposure–response analyses should consider intrinsic and extrinsic factors that may affect exposure and response.

findings.span: Dose–response and exposure–response analyses will be conducted only after completion of the Phase 2 expansion, with no interim reassessment planned as pharmacokinetic or clinical efficacy data accumulate.
findings.claim: Deferring these analyses until expansion is complete prevents emerging PK, efficacy, and safety evidence from informing dose selection or reassessment during development.
findings.guidance_quote: Dosage optimization should be an iterative process throughout drug development, using accumulating clinical and pharmacologic data.

findings.span: The combination expansion cohort will open after the first six participants complete cycle 1 of the investigational antibody plus pembrolizumab, without requiring prior monotherapy evaluation of the antibody at its recommended phase 2 dose.
findings.claim: The combination may expand after only a cycle-1 gate despite no required monotherapy evaluation of the investigational antibody; the protocol provides no basis for interpreting its contribution to combination toxicity.
findings.guidance_quote: Before initiating a combination expansion cohort, sponsors should have adequate information on the safety and pharmacokinetics of the investigational drug as a single agent and a rationale for the combination.

findings.span: The combination expansion cohort will open after the first six participants complete cycle 1 of the investigational antibody plus pembrolizumab, without requiring prior monotherapy evaluation of the antibody at its recommended phase 2 dose.
findings.claim: The synopsis identifies DV-505 as the investigational product but introduces an investigational antibody without defining its role, dosage, or relationship to DV-505; the combination cohort is therefore not operationally specified.
findings.guidance_quote: The trial protocol should be clear, concise, and operationally feasible.

findings.span: The pediatric expansion cohort will proceed under the adult development plan, with pediatric assessments documented separately and added to the pediatric study plan after the cohort is completed.
findings.claim: Pediatric-specific assessments and their development plan are deferred until after pediatric participants have been studied, rather than prospectively defining how their risks and outcomes will be assessed.
findings.guidance_quote: Clinical trials should be designed and conducted in ways that ensure the rights, safety, and well-being of participants and the reliability of trial results.

findings.span: Inclusion: age ≥18; histologically confirmed KRAS G12D-mutated locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor; ECOG 0–1; at least one prior line of systemic therapy; recovery of prior-treatment toxicities to Grade ≤1.
findings.claim: The age criterion makes the stated pediatric expansion cohort ineligible to enroll under this protocol.
findings.guidance_quote: The trial protocol should be clear, concise, and operationally feasible.

findings.span: Tumor biopsies will be collected during the expansion phase, with specimen handling procedures and biomarker testing and analysis methods to be finalized after enrollment begins.
findings.claim: Deferring specimen handling and biomarker methods until after enrollment risks inconsistent samples and uninterpretable PD or biomarker comparisons used for dose optimization.
findings.guidance_quote: Critical to quality factors should be identified prospectively, during study planning.

findings.span: The sponsor will include serious and unexpected adverse safety findings in the next scheduled annual safety report, unless the medical monitor requests earlier submission.
findings.claim: Discretionary reporting at the next annual report cannot replace expedited reporting of reportable suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions.
findings.guidance_quote: The sponsor should expedite the reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions to the relevant regulatory authorities and other parties as required by applicable regulatory requirements.

findings.span: Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle.
findings.claim: The visit schedule omits Cycle 1 Days 2 and 16, although intensive PK sampling requires a 24-hour post-dose sample after both Day 1 and Day 15.
findings.guidance_quote: The trial protocol should be clear, concise, and operationally feasible.

findings.span: Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts.
findings.claim: The protocol requires two intensive sampling days, each extending to a next-day sample, for every escalation participant without explaining why this burden is necessary across all participants.
findings.guidance_quote: The burden to participants should be considered when designing and conducting the trial.
